evidence: CancelOrderUseCase.ts execute(): returns an inline literal { id: order.id, status: order.getStatus(), lines: order.lines, createdAt: order.createdAt.toISOString() }
ListOrdersByStatusUseCase.ts execute(): orders.map(order => ({ id, status: order.getStatus(), lines, createdAt: order.createdAt.toISOString() })), the same mapping
PlaceOrderUseCase.ts private mapToDto(order: Order): OrderDto has the same mapping, but only this class uses it

parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module has one clear concern: application use cases for orders and stock. It still fails the rubric because it repeats rules that should live in one place. The Order→OrderDto mapping is written out by hand four times. PlaceOrderUseCase has a private mapToDto, but the other use cases do not use it and repeat the same object literal. UpdateOrderStatusUseCase keeps its own list of valid statuses. This repeats the OrderStatus type and the transition rules that Order.transitionTo already owns. The list also leaves out 'cancelled', which shows the two copies have already drifted apart. CancelOrderUseCase checks order.canBeCancelled() and releases stock, but it never moves the order to a cancelled status through the entity and never saves it, so it skips the module's own state-transition and persistence pattern. PlaceOrderUseCase checks order invariants itself (at least one line, quantity > 0) instead of leaving them to the Order entity.

violations.message: The Order→OrderDto mapping lives in a private mapToDto that other use cases can't reuse, so the rule is copied across the module. The order invariants (lines must not be empty, quantity > 0) are checked here instead of in the Order entity.

Repeats the inline Order→OrderDto mapping. It also releases stock without moving the order to a cancelled status through Order.transitionTo and without saving it through OrderRepository, so it skips the module's own state-transition and persistence pattern.
Repeats the inline Order→OrderDto mapping instead of using one shared mapper.
